newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden should be in ERM two yrs for EMU - Lamfalussy.
newsitem.headline: Sweden should be in ERM two yrs for EMU - Lamfalussy.

text.p: The head of the European Monetary Institute Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Monday Sweden should join the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) by year-end in order to qualify for membership of the EMU single currency.

"My opinion is that a country should be in the ERM for two years before it can enter the EMU, that is also the interpretation of the majority (of countries) of the convergence criteria," Lamfalussy said after an EMU seminar.
This would imply joining the ERM before the turn of the year, since the currency union is due to come into force on January 1, 1999.
Lamfalussy said there was a clear risk involved in not pegging the crown in the ERM if Sweden does intend to join the EMU from the start.
"That is my opinion, but the decision will ultimately be a political one," he said.
